done_when: The board shows the old-data line for a failed plan read, retries an item's first failed read straight away, and shows the newest failure reason.

known.title: Standard: Fake only third-party services at their edge
Follow-up: Retry reads for items absent from the Now snapshot

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Gate. Case: normal use - a plan or item read fails in the running board server. The standard says, “Fake only third-party services at their edge.” The plan scenario replaces the board's own `/plan/SHOP` response with a fabricated 500, and the item scenarios do the same for `/board.json?page=item` at lines 250 and 257. These tests would still pass if the real server returned a non-5xx response for those failures, which would prevent `Board.read` from reporting or retrying them. Exercise the failures through the running server so the named proofs cover the complete path.
findings.title: Standard: Fake only third-party services at their edge

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Test. Case: normal use - an item's first read fails and its retry succeeds. The test waits up to 60 seconds for the heading before checking that two requests occurred; it never establishes that the second request happened immediately. The installed clock is left running ([Playwright clock documentation](https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-clock#clock-pause-at)), so an implementation that waits 10 seconds before retrying would still satisfy these assertions. The proof needs to distinguish an immediate retry from the delayed behavior the fix replaces.
findings.title: Gate: tests/test_board_old_data_line_gaps.py::test_2_an_items_first_failed_read_is_asked_again_at_once_and_only_once

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 2, Harm 2
Case: normal use - someone opens an older item that the seven-day Now snapshot omits. After a plan read fails, this new `Board.read` records the failure, but the retry callback at `item.js:534-541` only rereads a page whose item is present in that snapshot. The plan and old-data line therefore remain in their failed state after the server recovers. The same condition leaves an older item's page or drawer in error if both immediate item reads fail (`item.js:234-243` and `315-321`).
Adds work: retry failed reads for open items outside the snapshot; F 1 x H 2 = 2; 2 x C = 4.
findings.title: Follow-up: Retry reads for items absent from the Now snapshot

stop.reason: The owner chose one more round: make the real board server fail in the tests and prove that the retry is at once

why: The old-data line is missing when a plan read fails, a first failed item read waits for the next snapshot instead of retrying at once, and a second failure with another reason keeps the first reason on the line.
